CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(20m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new PowerVar<VulnerablePower>(5m)` (Break.cs:19-23) == both numbers. Powered damage on both sides.

OnPlay.issue: The damage, the ordering and every amount are faithful; the divergence is the sim's extra `if not target.is_gone:` guard before the debuff. C# applies it unconditionally and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose doc comment states that dead creatures CAN still receive powers -- it refuses only when `CombatState == null` (the corpse was REMOVED) or ShouldAllowHitting says no. The two agree for an ordinary monster, because `CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `await Kill(...)` before returning (CreatureCmd.cs:409) and `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition` removes the creature at CreatureCmd.cs:523-525. They diverge for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; modelled in the sim as `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104, for ReattachPower/Decimillipede), because `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Observable through ViciousPower, which draws on any Vulnerable the owner applies with no liveness test on the target (ViciousPower.cs:19-26; sim port powers.py:1160-1179): hold Vicious, kill a retained-corpse enemy with this card -- the game draws, the sim does not. LIVE; card/vicious, ViciousPower and the retained-corpse path are all ported. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3). EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/card_probes.py dead-target-guards` lists 41 sim card classes that test liveness.

guards.rationale: AnyEnemy cards always resolve a target; `ctx.resolve_target(target_idx)` is the equivalent contract. Presentation, folded in: WithAttackerAnim / WithHitFx / WithHitVfxSpawnedAtBase and the Vulnerable hover tip.
